4: Pollock roe production for the A (January–May) and B (June–December) seasons, 2000–2026. At-sea Bering Sea inshore Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) data were included. Values are roe product metric tons. Open markers and dashed links identify provisional 2026 values through October 2026.
5: Spatial distribution of observed pollock catch in the A season (January 20–June 9), 2024–2026, in each year. Purple vertical bar height represents catch tons within 0.5-degree longitude by 0.25-degree latitude cells; the height scale is fixed across years within each season and a 10,000-t reference column in each panel. Data include available catcher-processor, mothership and observed catcher-vessel records in NMFS areas below 540. Electronic-monitoring catcher-vessel records are absent. The maps show observed-record catch totals rather than fleet-wide expanded catches. Blue shades show ocean depth and green shades show land elevation.
6: Spatial distribution of observed pollock catch in the B season (June 10–September 18), 2024–2026, in each year. Purple vertical bar height represents catch tons within 0.5-degree longitude by 0.25-degree latitude cells; the height scale is fixed across years within each season and a 10,000-t reference column in each panel. Data include available catcher-processor, mothership and observed catcher-vessel records in NMFS areas below 540. Electronic-monitoring catcher-vessel records are absent. The maps show observed-record catch totals rather than fleet-wide expanded catches. Blue shades show ocean depth and green shades show land elevation.
7: Fleet dispersion in the A and B seasons, 2000–2026 using a daily pairwise-distance approach. Unique tow pairs are formed within each day and vessel group (catcher-processors and observed catcher vessels); seasonal means pool distance sums and pair counts across both groups. No cross-group pairs are included. Distances are great-circle nautical miles. Solid lines use available seasonal records; dashed lines use records occurring between January 1 and September 18. The 2026 B season is partial. Tows included caught more than 80% pollock by catch weight, had valid locations, occurred in EBS reporting areas 500–539, and had tow durations between zero and 40 hours. Duration is calculated from timestamps with recorded minutes as fallback. Electronic-monitoring catcher-vessel records are absent.
8: Catch-weighted distributions of mean pollock weight per individual for A and B seasons, 1991–2026. Catch tons are grouped in 50-g bins; the vertical line marks 500 g. The 2026 B-season coverage includes data up to September 18. Available catcher-vessel records exclude electronic-monitoring records. Ridges describe the distribution of the mean individual weight by haul.
9: Weekly A-season (defined here as weeks 2–15) distributions of mean pollock weight, 2001–2026. Catch tons are grouped in approximately 66.7-g bins; the vertical line marks 500 g. Available catcher-vessel coverage is incomplete.
10: Weekly B-season (defined here as weeks 25–40) distributions of mean pollock weight, 2001–2026. Catch tons are grouped in approximately 66.7-g bins; the vertical line marks 500 g. The 2026 data include data through September 18 and therefore cover only part of this window. Available catcher-vessel coverage is incomplete.
11: Eastern Bering Sea pollock catch, 1964–2026, in million tons. Catches for 1964–1990 are undifferentiated by season and area; from 1991–2026 the A-season catches (January–June) are undifferentiated by area, while the B-season catches (June–December) are shown separately by area (NW and SE). The NW area comprises NMFS areas 520–529; SE comprises 500–517 and 519. The 2026 bar includes 1.268 million tons of catch through October 17 and is incomplete.
12: EBS bottom-trawl survey (BTS) pollock CPUE and bottom-temperature contours, 2018–2026 (no survey was conducted in 2020), reproduced from the AKsf R-package’s pollock-mapping example (Ianelli 2026). Blue points mark sampled tows; contours are labeled 0, 2 and 4 °C. Surfaces are descriptive local interpolations within survey coverage, with no spatial prediction intervals. The CPUE includes a density-dependent correction whose version and adoption status are unspecified in the example. The 2020 survey is absent.
